newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel mixed as sellers dominate.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel mixed as sellers dominate.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil market was mixed on Monday as sellers continued to offer large volumes while India's purchase of around 600,000 tonnes for March was largely ignored, traders said.
While gas oil swaps dipped from earlier levels, physical cargoes were offered higher.
By the end of the day, swaps gas oil for February was quoted at $25.70/$25.80 a barrel, down 25 cents from earlier levels while March was indicated at $26.00/$26.20.
Floating gas oil prices continued to be at a sharp discount to Singapore spot quotes while jet fuel commanded a premium of 30 cents per barrel.
A major continued to offer four cargoes for mid-to-second half February lifting at between $26.10 and $26.40 per barrel free-on-board basis, 10-40 cents over Friday's offers.
A trader also offered a Feb 11-15 lifting cargo at $25.80 a barrel, 60 cents over the deal done on Friday, with a bid seen at $25.30.

Traders noted that two majors who won India's tender might lift at least four cargoes due for deliveries to the Indian east coast from Singapore instead of the Mideast. This could help ease the current glut in supplies and support prices, they said.
But demand from China and Indonesia were thin.
Jet fuel prices continued to rise in relation to gas oil to over $3.00 a barrel, from around $2.60 last week.
